title: Throughput sanity and drift checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, runnable checklist for validating throughput runs and catching subtle drift/noise that wrecks repeatability. Designed as a light-weight complement to the larger benchmark harness docs (use when triaging flaky runs or shipping a new kernel/model combo).

Scope:
- Applies to steady-throughput and burst-style throughput experiments for the serving runtime (GPU-backed inference).
- Focuses on environmental priming, warmup, simple statistical sanity checks, and artifact collection for post-mortem.
- NOT a comprehensive profiling guide — see profiling playbook for perf traces.

When to use:
- New model or kernel drop landed on CI/dev fleet.
- Observed throughput regressions vs baseline.
- Preparing an SLO test for a customer-facing rollout.

Quick checklist (runnable):
1) Pre-flight (1–2m)
   - Confirm commit + model version: git rev / model tag. Record in run metadata.
   - Node health: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv` (expect stable readings, no thermal throttling).
   - Ensure no other heavy jobs: `ps aux | grep loadgen` / cluster scheduler check.
   - Check container image & runtime flags match baseline (quant/flags).

2) Deterministic seed & dataset (mandatory)
   - Use fixed loadgen seed and fixed prompt set (embed dataset id in metadata).
   - If using synthetic sequences, attach the generator seed and histogram.

3) Priming phase (3–6 min depending on model)
   - Goal: populate KV cache and GPU kernels, avoid first-epoch penalties.
   - Run a 3-minute priming stream at target concurrency with short prompts (to get hot paths).
   - Monitor token throughput and per-request latency; expect step-up over first minute, then plateau.

4) Warmup profile (10–20 min typical)
   - Run incremental throughput ramps: 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% of target QPS; hold 90–120s each.
   - Capture: per-second token/s, request latency P50/P90/P99, GPU util, memory, and host CPU.
   - Acceptable warmup: <10% variance across last two steps for token/s; latency stable within ±15% from P50 baseline.

5) Steady-state collection (10+ minutes recommended)
   - Run the target load for at least 10 minutes (longer for high-variance mixes).
   - Collect: time-series logs, loadgen seed, agent logs, kernel traces (if enabled), and perf counters (nvprof/nsys samples).

6) Drift & noise checks (post-run quick checks)
   - Run-to-run repeatability: repeat identical run 3x; compute mean and stddev of token/s. Flag if stddev/mean > 4%.
   - Sequence-length sensitivity: split results by sequence-length buckets (0-128, 129-512, 513+). Look for disproportionate variance.
   - Microburst sensitivity: inspect short-timescale (1s/500ms) token/s; if microbursts exceed sustained by >30% frequently, note possible batching instability.

7) Sanity assertions (auto-checks to run after each job)
   - No CUDA OOMs in logs.
   - Mean token/s within ±7% of expected baseline (unless baseline intentionally changed).
   - P99 latency does not exceed SLO threshold (configurable per-run).
   - GPU memory footprint stable across run (no creeping allocations).

8) Artifact collection (mandatory attachments)
   - loadgen config file (JSON) used for run.
   - aggregated metrics CSV (timestamp, token/s, QPS, P50/P90/P99).
   - nsys/strace/ktrace snippets if enabled (time-aligned).
   - container runtime logs and kernel log.
   - model binary + quant flags + compile flags.

9) Quick triage script (1–2 cmds)
   - Extract summary: `jq -r '.metrics | {mean_tokens, stddev_tokens, p99_latency}' run_output.json`
   - Compare to baseline: `python tools/compare_runs.py baseline.json run_output.json --threshold 0.07`

Expected failure modes & first actions:
- High variance between runs: suspect noisy infra (background jobs) or non-deterministic scheduling; repro on a reserved single-node instance.
- Latency spike at start then stable: insufficient priming; increase priming duration or warmup steps.
- Steady drift downward: memory leak or allocator fragmentation — collect `malloc` stats and heap profile.
- Microbursts: mis-sized batching window or bad backpressure; inspect batching histograms and client pacing.

Guidance for experimental knobs:
- Batching window: prefer conservative (smaller) for low-latency SLO tests, measure cost impact separately.
- KV cache policy: for long-chat workloads, priming must include representative history lengths.
- Quantization changes: run side-by-side with float baseline on the same node to isolate model vs runtime regression.

Lightweight reproducible recipe (single node dev):
1) Reserve a dev SKU with 1 GPU and identical image.
2) Copy promptset: `gsutil cp gs://bench-data/promptsets/latest.json ./prompts.json`
3) Run priming: `./loadgen --seed=42 --prompts=prompts.json --concurrency=8 --duration=180 --mode=prime`
4) Warmup ramp: `./loadgen --ramp 25,50,75,100 --hold 90 --seed=42 --prompts=prompts.json`
5) Collect: `tar -czf artifacts.tgz metrics.csv logs/ nsys.qdrep`

Notes / gotchas (first-hand):
- CI runners with co-located monitors (e.g., metrics exporters writing to disk) introduced 2–3% noise spikes — isolate exporters or run on dedicated dev nodes when comparing small deltas.
- For multi-GPU model parallel runs, clock-domain sync issues caused small periodic stalls. Check kernel launch timestamps if you see periodic cadence in token/s.
- Some quantized kernels show lower variance but shifted medians; always compare both mean and percentiles.

Follow-ups after a flagged run:
- Reproduce on an isolated reserved node. If still fails, collect full perf traces and open JIRA with tags: eng-serving-runtime, perf-regression, noisy-run. Attach artifacts and the 3 run outputs.
- If isolated run passes, schedule infra/mesh investigation (possible noisy neighbor).

TODOs / runway improvements:
- Add an automated microburst detector to the harness and fail runs that exceed microburst thresholds.
- Record hardware topology and PCIe link speeds in run metadata for better triage.
- Integrate lightweight heap sampling at the end of each long run to catch creeping allocations.

Appendix: quick-check commands (copyable)
- Node snapshot: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 --filename node_snapshot.csv &`
- Loadgen replay (same seed): `./loadgen --replay runX.load --seed=42`
- Extract 1s token/s series: `python tools/parse_metrics.py --input metrics.json --granularity 1s --metric tokens_per_sec > tokens_1s.csv`

If you add or change a warmup parameter, append a short note here with reason and reference ticket.

Author notes (Maya):
- I created this checklist after chasing a 6% regression that evaporated when runs were moved to reserved nodes. The checklist is intentionally terse so it can be pasted into run reports or JIRA reproduction steps.
summary: Compact, runnable checklist for throughput run sanity, warmup, drift detection, and artifact collection. Intended for quick triage of flaky or regressing throughput experiments.
